name: ReMe (Remember Me, Refine Me): A Dynamic Procedural Memory Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution
venue: ACL 2026 Findings (accepted; 'ACL'26-Findings' noted on arXiv). Preprint arXiv:2512.10696 (cs.AI / cs.CL), v1 submitted 11 Dec 2025, v2 last revised 15 Apr 2026.
authors_affiliation: Zouying Cao (lead; AGI Institute, School of Computer Science, Shanghai Jiao Tong University; work done during internship at Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group), Jiaji Deng, Li Yu, Weikang Zhou, Zhaoyang Liu (corresponding), Bolin Ding (Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group), Hai Zhao (corresponding; Shanghai Jiao Tong University). Primary affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group. Contact: zouyingcao@sjtu.edu.cn, zhaohai@cs.sjtu.edu.cn.
code_url: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe (official; part of the AgentScope ecosystem, ~3.1k stars, 851 commits, actively maintained, last commit 2026-06-05). The paper also releases the reme.library procedural-memory dataset.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe (continuously-updated open-source memory framework; supports personal / procedural / tool memory types, MCP client, and multiple agent backends such as AgentScope and the Claude Code SDK; broader than the frozen paper).
task_domain: Tool-use / function-calling and interactive coding agents (decision-making over multi-turn agentic tool execution). Framed as a procedural-memory system for LLM agents that internalizes 'how-to' knowledge to improve task-solving.
problem_setting: Single-agent, experience-driven self-evolution for LLM tool-use agents. The setting is two-phase: (1) an offline experience-acquisition phase where an execution agent interacts with the environment over a set of TRAINING tasks (50 BFCL-V3 base multi-turn tasks; 90 AppWorld train tasks), sampling N=8 trajectories per task at temperature 0.9 to obtain success/failure pairs, which a summarizer LLM distills into a structured experience pool; (2) a test-time reuse/refinement phase on held-out tasks (150 BFCL-V3 eval, 168 AppWorld test-normal) where relevant experiences are retrieved and injected, and the pool is optionally updated online (ReMe-dynamic vs ReMe-fixed). No gradient training of the agent or retriever; everything is LLM-driven in-context with frozen off-the-shelf embeddings. Backbones are swapped (Qwen3-8B/14B/32B-Instruct as both execution and summarizer LLM; plus GPT-4.1, o4-mini, Qwen3-Max-Preview, Kimi-K2-Thinking, DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-4.7 for generalization). Task success uses environment ground truth (BFCL-V3 AST+execution checks; AppWorld state-based unit tests / Task Goal Completion). Contrasted against the 'passive accumulation' append-only memory paradigm.
what_is_retrieved: Distilled, structured procedural experiences (not raw trajectories). Each experience E = <omega, e, kappa, c, tau> bundles a usage scenario omega (when to use it), the core experience content e, a set of categorization keywords kappa, a confidence score c in [0,1], and the set of tools tau used. Experiences come in three multi-faceted types: success patterns, failure-trigger lessons, and comparative insights distilled jointly from paired success/failure trajectories.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic self-written procedural memory (experience pool). ReMe maintains no static external doc/KB/API corpus; the retrievable store is an agent-written experience pool seeded offline from training-task trajectories and (in the dynamic variant) grown/pruned online at test time. Positioned explicitly against static append-only memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-K ranking objective. Retrieval selects the top-K=5 most relevant experiences by cosine similarity over the usage-scenario embedding (then optional rerank/rewrite). There is no minimal-complete-set or variable-size precision-driven objective; the K-sweep (K=0..10) shows performance rising then saturating/declining with larger K (noise tradeoff), motivating moderate K.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (top-K cosine retrieval over usage-scenario embeddings, plus optional LLM reranking); Reuse: yes (retrieved experiences injected as in-context demonstrations, with an adaptive rewriting module that reorganizes them into task-specific guidance); Revise: yes (context-adaptive rewriting adapts retrieved experiences to the new task; failure-aware reflection revises strategy after a failed attempt); Retain: yes (utility-based refinement: selective addition of validated successful experiences, failure-reflection-derived lessons on success, and utility-based pruning of stale entries)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as a 'procedural memory' / 'experience-driven agent evolution' framework and positions against memory systems (A-Mem, LangMem, AWM, Agent KB, CER, Synapse, HiAgent). It does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner and does not use the term 'case-based reasoning'; it realizes Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain-like mechanisms under a memory-lifecycle framing.
retrieval_unit: guideline/insight-level procedural experience (a distilled 'keypoint-level' experience), structured as E=<usage-scenario omega, core content e, keywords kappa, confidence c, tools tau>. It is finer-grained than a full trajectory or whole-trajectory workflow: a reusable success pattern, failure-trigger lesson, or comparative insight. The granularity ablation explicitly contrasts this keypoint-level unit against a trajectory-level unit.
index_source: Hybrid offline-then-online growing memory. The pool is offline-induced from training-task exploration trajectories (experience acquisition), then for ReMe(dynamic) is online/test-time-induced: validated successful experiences are added and low-utility ones pruned during deployment. ReMe(fixed) freezes the pool after offline induction. Stored in a vector database.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index. Each retained experience is indexed by the embedding vector of its usage-scenario field omega and stored in a vector database (experience pool); retrieval is nearest-neighbor by cosine similarity. Keywords kappa support categorization/metadata. No explicit dependency/knowledge graph or hierarchical category tree is used for the procedural pool (the broader open-source framework adds personal/tool memory types, but the paper's procedural pool is a flat scenario-keyed vector index).
retriever_type: Dense (embedding-based) retriever using cosine similarity over usage-scenario embeddings, plus an OPTIONAL LLM-as-reranker stage (LLM_rerank). Embeddings come from an off-the-shelf text embedding model (text-embedding-v4, dim 1024, in main experiments; Qwen3-Embedding cited as an alternative). No BM25 and no learned/generative retriever; the only learned component used at selection time is the LLM reranker (zero-shot prompted, not trained).
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf). The dense retriever uses a frozen pretrained embedding model (text-embedding-v4 / Qwen3-Embedding) with cosine similarity; there is no contrastive fine-tuning, LM-feedback retriever training, or RL/value-based retrieval learning. The closest thing to a downstream-effectiveness signal is the separate utility-based DELETION mechanism (tracks per-experience recall-to-success utility u/f and prunes below threshold beta), but this prunes the store rather than training the retriever.
query_construction: Raw current-task query embedded with the same embedding model and matched against experience usage-scenario embeddings. The retrieval-key ablation shows the STORED key is an LLM-generated 'usage scenario' field (omega), which outperforms indexing by raw task description, generalized query, or extracted query keywords. So query construction = raw task query on the read side; the value-add is LLM-generated scenario indexing on the write/key side.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0). Retrieval is performed once at the beginning of each task to fetch the top-K experiences; not per-CoT-step or per-tool-call. The Limitations section explicitly notes the fixed once-per-task retrieval as a constraint, suggesting future context-aware re-retrieval.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot per task. Experiences are retrieved exactly once at the start of each task (matched for all methods for fair comparison). No iterative, uncertainty-triggered, or learned-router re-retrieval within a task. (The dynamic variant updates the POOL after task execution, but does not re-retrieve mid-task.)
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule. Retrieval is triggered unconditionally once at the beginning of each new task. There is no token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated mid-step retrieval trigger. (The failure-aware reflection that re-triggers a new trial is a refinement/re-execution trigger, not a re-retrieval trigger.)
reranking: Yes (optional). After dense top-K retrieval, an optional context-aware LLM reranker (LLM_rerank) re-evaluates experience relevance against the current task's specific context, constraints, and objectives, bringing the most pertinent experiences to the front. It is a zero-shot LLM-as-reranker (instruction-prompted), not a trained cross-encoder or RRF. Ablation (Table 4, Qwen3-8B, BFCL-V3): +ReMe 27.17 Avg@4/34.66 Pass@4 -> +rerank 28.91/36.67; rerank+rewrite together reach 29.00/40.67.
retrieved_context_refinement: Rerank + adaptive rewrite (decompose-then-recompose into task-specific guidance). Beyond optional reranking, a rewriting module reorganizes the multiple retrieved experiences into a single cohesive, task-specific guidance more directly applicable to the new task. This is post-retrieval refinement of the fetched set (not compression/distractor-filtering per se). Write-time refinement (multi-faceted distillation, LLM-as-Judge validation, similarity-based dedup) also reduces noise before items enter the pool.
tool_document_engineering: N/A. ReMe retrieves distilled procedural experiences, not tool/API descriptions, so there is no tool-docstring indexing pipeline. (Each experience records the tools tau it used, but tools are not the retrievable items.)
index_content_separation: Partial. Each experience separates a lightweight retrievable key (the usage-scenario embedding omega + keywords kappa) from the heavier core content e injected on use, but there is no explicit progressive-disclosure / index-then-load-content mechanism for the procedural pool.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A for the paper's procedural pool (a static vector DB, no external live tool registry/integration protocol). The broader open-source ReMe framework does include an MCP client and tool-memory components, but the paper does not evaluate a live-synchronized tool index or MCP/RapidAPI/RESTful protocol. [uncertain]
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A. ReMe does not model inter-tool dependencies (it is an experience/procedural-memory method, not a tool-retrieval method). Experiences record which tools tau were used but do not encode tool dependency graphs.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation (in-context demonstrations). The top-K retrieved (and reranked) experiences are rewritten into task-specific guidance and concatenated into the execution agent's context as in-context-learning demonstrations to guide reasoning and tool calls. No fine-tuning and no latent-token injection; everything is in-context.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan, one-shot at task start. Relevant experiences are retrieved once and injected before the agent begins its multi-turn ReAct-style tool-use rollout, acting as one-shot strategic exemplars/guidance for the whole task. Not interleaved per-step, not inside MCTS/tree search. A failure-aware reflection loop (max 3 self-reflections) can re-execute a failed task with extracted lessons, which is a retry/refinement loop on top of the plan.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-task / per-answer. Retrieval and experience injection happen once before the agent's rollout and remain fixed for that task; not per-CoT-step, per-token, or per-tool-call.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation plus execution-feedback-driven revision: (1) the rewriting module (LLM) reorganizes retrieved experiences into cohesive task-specific guidance (context-adaptive reuse); (2) the failure-aware reflection mechanism (LLM_summ analyzes a failed attempt, extracts improvement lessons, then LLM_execute starts a new trial on those lessons; lessons retained only if the retry succeeds, max 3 reflections). Not verbatim ICL, not RL reuse-finetuning, not latent.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled structured experience injected as free-text guidance: a structured record (usage scenario, core content, keywords, confidence, tools) that the rewriting module turns into cohesive task-specific natural-language guidance. Not raw trajectories, executable programs, or latent/soft tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled strategy / state-aware guideline (keypoint-level). Above a raw logged trajectory: reusable success patterns, failure-trigger lessons, and comparative insights, each tagged with a usage scenario stating WHEN to apply it. The granularity ablation shows this keypoint-level abstraction substantially outperforms trajectory-level experiences (Table 2).
noise_robustness_mechanism: (1) LLM-as-a-Judge validation filters out non-actionable/inaccurate experiences before storage; (2) similarity-based cosine deduplication discards redundant experiences to preserve diversity; (3) multi-faceted distillation (success/failure/comparative) yields fine-grained keypoint experiences rather than noisy raw trajectories; (4) optional LLM reranking selects the most contextually relevant experiences; (5) utility-based deletion prunes frequently-retrieved-but-unhelpful (toxic) experiences (u/f <= beta after >= alpha retrievals); (6) selective addition (success-only at test time) avoids low-quality single-failure experiences; (7) moderate K=5 limits noisy-experience injection. No retriever-aware contrastive training.
memory_type: Procedural memory (experience pool / skill-like reusable how-to knowledge), realized as a flat scenario-keyed vector store of distilled experiences. Not parametric, not a knowledge graph, not latent. (The broader framework also supports personal and tool memory types, but the paper studies procedural memory.)
write_back: Yes. New validated experiences are written into the pool. Offline: multi-faceted distillation of training trajectories -> LLM-as-Judge validation -> dedup -> store, indexed by usage-scenario embedding. Online (ReMe-dynamic): selective addition of experiences from newly successful trajectories and from successful failure-reflection retries; plus utility-based deletion of stale entries. Closed loop: distill -> validate -> dedup -> store -> reuse -> track utility -> prune.
online_growth: Yes for ReMe(dynamic): the pool grows (selective addition) and shrinks (utility-based deletion) during deployment as tasks are executed. ReMe(fixed) freezes the pool after offline induction (the fixed-vs-dynamic comparison is a core contribution; dynamic consistently outperforms fixed across all model sizes and benchmarks).
write_back_trigger: On-success (selective addition) plus reflective on failure with success-gating. The paper compares full addition (add from all trajectories regardless of outcome) vs selective addition (add only from successful trajectories) and finds selective addition superior because a single test-time failed trajectory gives insufficient context for reliable failure analysis. A failure-aware reflection branch lets the agent retry a failed task; the derived lessons are written back ONLY if the retry succeeds, otherwise discarded. Initial offline pool also draws failure/comparative experiences (from collectively analyzed failures). Validation (LLM-as-Judge) and dedup gate every write.
failure_experience_usage: Success+failure contrastive, with asymmetric handling. During OFFLINE acquisition, ReMe uses multi-faceted distillation: success-pattern recognition, failure analysis (failure-trigger lessons identifying the earliest key step leading to suboptimal outcomes), and comparative insight generation from paired highest/lowest-reward trajectories. During ONLINE refinement, however, failure experiences are NOT directly added (selective/success-only addition); instead failures trigger a self-reflection retry loop and lessons are kept only upon subsequent success. So failures are used contrastively/correctively but gated to avoid toxic single-failure noise.
memory_evolution_update: Refine-and-prune: selective append of validated successful experiences (with similarity-based dedup-merge to avoid redundancy) plus utility-based forget/prune of low-utility entries. ReMe tracks per-experience total retrievals f and historical utility u (u increments when a recall contributes to a successful task); an experience is removed when, after >= alpha=5 retrievals, u/f <= beta=0.5. Not append-only; combines dedup-merge and forget-prune. (Individual stored experiences are not rewritten in place after storage; evolution is at the pool level via add/dedup/delete plus the test-time rewriting that adapts them on use.)
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Experience selection is fixed cosine-similarity top-K over frozen embeddings, with an optional zero-shot LLM reranker; it is not an RL- or value-trained retrieval policy. Utility tracking (u/f) drives pool PRUNING, not a learned retrieval policy. (This is an explicit contrast with M-MDP/soft-Q or RL-retrieval methods such as Memento/ARTIST-style learned case selection.)
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: In the paper: single-agent private procedural memory (one execution agent self-evolves its own pool; summarizer = execution model). The released open-source framework is designed as a reusable memory service with multiple agent backends (AgentScope, Claude Code SDK) and an MCP client, enabling experience reuse across agent frameworks in principle, but the paper does not study cross-agent experience sharing. [uncertain]
benchmarks: BFCL-V3 (Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard V3; >1,800 test tasks for multi-turn/multi-step function calling; AST matching + executable testing; ReMe uses 50 base multi-turn tasks for the initial pool and 150 for evaluation; full multi-turn category = 750 tasks split Base 150 / Miss Param 200 / Miss Func 200 / Long Context 200) and AppWorld (controllable world of 9 apps, 457 APIs, ~100 simulated users; state-based unit tests; ReMe uses 90 train tasks and 168 test-normal tasks; reports Task Goal Completion). Backbones: Qwen3-8B/14B/32B-Instruct (main), plus GPT-4.1, o4-mini, Qwen3-Max-Preview, Kimi-K2-Thinking, DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-4.7 (generalization on BFCL-V3).
benchmark_family: tool (function-calling / interactive coding agents): BFCL-V3 = tool / function-calling (ToolBench-adjacent agentic tool-use), AppWorld = tool + code (interactive coding agent over app APIs). No QA, web, embodied, memory-conversation, or decision-RL benchmarks.
baselines: No Memory (vanilla backbone, no memory mechanism); A-Mem (Xu et al. 2025; agentic memory / memory-centric knowledge graph, reproduced with slight prompt modifications to extract procedural memories); LangMem (LangChain 2025; long-term episodic memory module that extracts info from conversations and refines prompts). Two ReMe variants are reported: ReMe(fixed) (frozen pool) and ReMe(dynamic) (online refinement). For fairness all methods retrieve once per task start and add memory only on successful trajectories.
key_metrics: Avg@4 (average task success rate over 4 independent trials) and Pass@4 (probability >=1 of 4 trials succeeds); all results averaged over 3 independent runs with standard deviation. For AppWorld the underlying metric is Task Goal Completion (TGC); for BFCL-V3, AST + executable correctness. Efficiency: average inference latency per task. Error analysis: failure-case counts by error category (Reasoning Error, Action Omission, etc.).
headline_result: ReMe sets new SOTA agent-memory results on BFCL-V3 and AppWorld and shows a memory-scaling effect: Qwen3-8B + ReMe(dynamic) outperforms larger memoryless Qwen3-14B (avg Pass@4 55.03% vs 54.65%; and Qwen3-8B + ReMe(dynamic) average Avg@4 34.94 / Pass@4 55.03 vs No-Memory 27.65 / 46.20). Reported headline gains for Qwen3-8B + ReMe over No Memory: +8.83% Avg@4 and +7.29% Pass@4 on average across BFCL-V3+AppWorld. On Qwen3-14B, ReMe(dynamic) avg Avg@4 44.66 / Pass@4 63.71 exceeds memoryless Qwen3-32B (40.89 / 61.52).
ablations: (1) Granularity (Table 2): keypoint-level experiences vs trajectory-level: Qwen3-8B 44.50/65.77 vs 43.00/60.00 Avg@4/Pass@4; Qwen3-14B 51.89/72.44 vs 49.66/69.33; keypoint-level gives substantially larger gains over No Memory. (2) Component (Table 3, Qwen3-8B BFCL-V3): full addition 40.83/62.00 -> selective addition 44.33/64.66 (+3.50/+2.66) -> +failure-aware reflection 45.00/64.66 -> +utility-based deletion 45.17/68.00; quality>quantity, and pruning matters in non-stationary settings. (3) Rerank/Rewrite (Table 4, Qwen3-8B no-thinking): +ReMe 27.17/34.66 -> +rerank 28.91/36.67, +rewrite 28.67/37.33, both 29.00/40.67. (4) Retrieval-key (Fig 4 / Table 8-style): usage-scenario indexing best, beating raw task query / generalized query / query keywords (Qwen3-8B usage scenario 44.50/65.77). (5) Summarizer scaling (Table 5): stronger LLM_summ (8B->32B, fixed 8B executor) lifts Avg@4 +1.83%->+3.33%, Pass@4 +0.23%->+2.23%. (6) Effect of K (Fig 5): performance rises then saturates, K=5 chosen. (7) Error analysis (Fig 6): failures 62->47, corrects 17 baseline errors / introduces 2, Reasoning Errors 22->14.
evaluation_decoupling: No. ReMe reports only end-to-end task metrics (Avg@4/Pass@4 success rates) and does not report intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG/completeness) for the experience retriever. Retrieval design is studied via downstream task accuracy in the retrieval-key and K-number ablations rather than via decoupled IR metrics.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-based (task success Avg@4/Pass@4). A qualitative process analysis is provided via the error-type breakdown (Reasoning Error, Action Omission, etc.) showing where ReMe reduces failures, and case studies/experience examples, but no quantitative step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or trajectory-quality score is reported.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported as favorable. On AppWorld, average inference latency per task: No Memory 21.42s vs +ReMe 23.96s (+2.54s), deemed an acceptable overhead. The headline efficiency claim is the memory-scaling effect: a smaller model + ReMe matches/exceeds a larger memoryless model, framed as a computation-efficient pathway to lifelong learning. No token-count or API-cost table is reported. Acquisition cost: N=8 trajectory samples per training task and up to 3 self-reflection retries per failed task.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed top-K=5 retrieved experiences per task (after optional reranking and rewriting into a single cohesive guidance block). K is fixed (not adaptive/precision-driven); the K=0..10 sweep shows saturation, justifying K=5. Agent rollout capped at max 30 iterations; self-reflection capped at 3. No explicit injected-token budget is reported.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (ReMe is a method/framework, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (ReMe is a method, not a benchmark). It does release the reme.library procedural-memory dataset (fine-grained experiences with structured success patterns and failure lessons distilled from diverse agentic tasks) as a community resource, but the paper does not frame this as a scored benchmark. [uncertain]
builds_on: Procedural/experience memory for agents: ExpEL (experiential learners), Reflexion (verbal self-reflection retry, cited for the max-3 reflections choice), Agent Workflow Memory (AWM), Agent KB (cross-domain experience, teacher-student dual retrieval), CER (Contextual Experience Replay, fine-grained skills), Synapse and HiAgent (trajectory-as-exemplar memory). Uses LLM-as-a-Judge (Zheng et al. 2023) for validation, Qwen3 models, and off-the-shelf embeddings (text-embedding-v4 / Qwen3-Embedding). Builds on the experience-following-behavior study (Xiong et al. 2025) for utility-based deletion thresholds.
contrasts_with: Static 'passive accumulation' append-only memory systems: A-Mem and LangMem (its main empirical baselines), and trajectory-level / whole-trajectory-workflow memory (Synapse, HiAgent, AWM, Agent KB, CER) which store coarse experiences without adaptation or timely pruning. ReMe contrasts by (a) keypoint-level multi-faceted distillation vs raw/whole-trajectory storage, (b) context-adaptive reuse (rerank+rewrite) vs unadapted injection, and (c) utility-based refinement (add valid, prune stale) vs append-only growth.
lineage: Group F (decision/experience/procedural memory for self-evolving agents). A 2025-2026 dynamic-procedural-memory work in the lineage of experience-learning agents (Reflexion -> ExpEL -> AWM / Agent KB / CER) that extends them with a closed-loop, utility-driven, self-pruning memory lifecycle; a non-RL, in-context experience-reuse method (contrast with RL-policy case-selection lines such as Memento).
